dedupe_keys.name: fire service gap analysis based on isochrone maps in dki jakarta fire stations incidents 2024 2025 and blank spots

description: This data set maps where fire engines in Jakarta, Indonesia, can and cannot reach within a few minutes, to find neighbourhoods left outside fast fire response. The producers are Vian Azis Tio Riwanto, Richo Thomas Arnando and Muhammad Akmal Syafi'i of Binus University, who built a web GIS for fire service gap analysis. Coverage is the Special Capital Region of Jakarta, with 174 active fire stations and fire incidents from 2024 and 2025. The workbooks, in English and Indonesian, give administrative boundaries, station coordinates and incident records; a zipped set of GeoJSON layers holds merged drive-time polygons around stations at four, five and seven minutes and the resulting blank spots. The deposit also includes diagrams of the system, which uses a cloud database and a large language model assistant, and results of user testing. The files are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the routing source and traffic assumptions behind the isochrones are not stated in the deposit, incident records may be incomplete, and the system relies on commercial cloud services. Simulation uses: testing new fire station locations, estimating how congestion or flooding in Jakarta shrinks response coverage, and linking incident density to service gaps. Related records: the US fire department registry (data-usfa-national-fire-department-registry) lists stations in the United States, and the San Francisco fire and EMS calls (data-sf-fire-ems-calls-for-service) give detailed response records.
